# Saba's Cleaned data
```{r Cleaning data}
#Downloading dataset with relevant columns only
smarvus_raw <- read.csv("smarvus_correct_cols.csv")

# Remove participants with no reported grade data or where grade has been reported as 0
smarvus_raw <- smarvus_raw |>
  filter(!grade %in% c(
    "Not Available", 
    NA, 
    "Non complete - LoA", 
    "No stats module on record", 
    "No stats modules", 
    "No access to transcript",
    "-",
    "0",
    "0.00",
    "0%",
    "0.00%"
  ))

# Remove participants who did not answer the anxiety questions 
anxiety_cols <- c(
  paste0("Q7.1_", 1:23),
  paste0("Q7.2_", 1:19),
  paste0("Q8.1_", 1:20),
  paste0("Q8.2_", 1:20)
)

smarvus_filtered <- smarvus_raw |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(anxiety_cols), ~ !is.na(.)))

# Grouping England and Northern Ireland into one country
smarvus_filtered <- smarvus_filtered |>
  mutate(country = if_else(
    country %in% c("England", "Northern Ireland"),
    "United Kingdom",
    country
  ))

before <- nrow(smarvus_filtered)

smarvus_filtered <- smarvus_filtered |>
  filter(
    attention_amnesty == "Yes",
    Q7.1_24 == "1",
    Q8.1_21 == "5",
    Q9.1_22 == "1",
    Q11.1_9 == "3",
    Q13.1_17 == "2",
    Q15.1_9 == "4"
  )

# Number of respondents removed
before - nrow(smarvus_filtered)

# Number of respondents remaining
nrow(smarvus_filtered)


```

```{r Stats anxiety score}
# STARS
stars_cols <- paste0("Q7.1_", 1:23)

# R-MARS
rmars_cols <- paste0("Q8.2_", 1:20)

# STARS-M
stars_m_cols <- c(
  paste0("Q8.1_", 1:20),
  "Q7.1_9", "Q7.1_12", "Q7.1_17"
)

# R-MARS-S
rmars_s_cols <- c(
  paste0("Q7.2_", 1:19),
  "Q8.2_11"
)

# Calculate scores
smarvus_filtered <- smarvus_filtered |>
  mutate(
    stars_score = rowSums(pick(all_of(stars_cols))),
    rmars_score = rowSums(pick(all_of(rmars_cols))),
    stars_m_score = rowSums(pick(all_of(stars_m_cols))),
    rmars_s_score = rowSums(pick(all_of(rmars_s_cols)))
  )
```

# Old

```{r Defining grade bands}
# In all cases grade assigned is by taking the mid point of the grade band

# ==================================
# brawijaya conversion
# "A > 80, 75 < B+ ≤ 80, 69 < B ≤ 75, 60 < C+ ≤ 69, 55 < C ≤ 60, 50 < D+ ≤ 55, 44 < D ≤ 50, E < 44"     
brawijaya_conversion_old <- c(
  "A"  = 90,
  "B+" = 77.5, "B"  = 72,
  "C+" = 64.5, "C"  = 57.5,
  "D+" = 52.5,"D"  = 47,
  "E"  = 22     
)

# ==================================
# limerik
# taking the mid point of the grade band
# ">80 = A1, 75-79 = A2, 70-74 = B1, 65-69 = B2, 60-64 = B3, 55-59 = C1, 50-54 = C2, 45-49 = C3,
# 40-44 = D1, 35-39 = D2, <35 = F
limerick_conversion_old <- c(
  "A1"  = 90, "A2" = 77, 
  "B1"  = 73, "B2" = 67, "B3" = 62,
  "C1" = 57, "C2"  = 52, "C3" = 47,
  "D1" = 42, "D2"  = 37,
  "F"  = 17.5     
)

# ==================================
# mef
# taking the mid point of the grade band
# "A = 90-100, A- = 80-89, B+ = 75-79, B = 70-74, B- = 65-69; C+ = 60-64, C = 55-59, C- = 50-54, 
# D+ = 45-49, D = 35-44, F <35"   
mef_conversion_old <- c(
  "A"  = 95, "A-" = 84.5, 
  "B+"  = 77, "B" = 72, "B-" = 67,
  "C+" = 62, "C"  = 57, "C-" = 52,
  "D+" = 47, "D"  = 39.5,
  "F"  = 17.5     
)

# ==================================
# york_can
# conversion not given- https://calendars.students.yorku.ca/2025-2026/grades-and-grading-schemes

york_can_conversion_old <- c(
  "A+" = 95, "A" = 84.5,
  "B+" = 77.5, "B" = 72.5,
  "C+" = 67.5, "C" = 62.5,
  "D+" = 57.5, "D" = 42.5,
  "E" = 44.5, "F" = 17.5,
  
  # For the following grades, couldn't find on the internet what they meant 
  # so computed them by generating the boundary they are in and found the midpt
  
  # EG: for this one B+ in (75,79) and D+ in (55,59), 
  # so treaded B+, D+ as being in (55,79) so midpt of 67
  
  "B+, D+" = 67, 
  "A, A+" = 94.5,
  "A+, A+" = 95,
  "A, C+" = 77,
  "C+, C" = 64.5,
  "C+, A" = 77,
  "A+, B" = 85,
  "B, B" = 72.5 
)

# ==================================
# All remaining universities grades are already numeric

numeric_grade <- function(df) {df %>%
  mutate(
    grade = as.character(grade),
    grade_std = case_when(
      
      # anglia_ruskin and sussex: Grades with "%" in them
      survey_id %in% c("anglia_ruskin", "sussex") ~
        suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("%", "", grade))),

      # brawijaya conversion
      survey_id %in% "brawijaya" ~
        unname(brawijaya_conversion[grade]),

      # limerick
      survey_id %in% "limerick" ~
        unname(limerick_conversion[grade]),
      
      # mef
      survey_id %in% "mef" ~
        unname(mef_conversion[grade]),  
      
      # york_can
      survey_id %in% "york_can" ~
        unname(york_can_conversion[grade]),

      # All other universities stay the same
      survey_id %in% c("bournemouth", "bradford", 
                       "hasan_kalyoncu", "hungary",
                        "la_laguna", "lincoln_1", 
                        "lincoln_2", "macquarie",
                        "queens", "rotterdam", 
                        "southampton", "teesside",
                        "uc_louvain", "vienna", 
                        "western_aus_a", "western_aus_b") ~
        suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grade)),

    )
  )
}

```

# Function

```{r Making grades numeric in df}
# Making all grade numeric respective to their individual coversions
numeric_to_ordinal_grade <- function(df) {df %>%
  mutate(
    grade = as.character(grade),
    grade_std = case_when(
      
      # anglia_ruskin and sussex: Grades with "%" in them
      survey_id %in% c("anglia_ruskin", "sussex") ~
        suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sub("%", "", grade))),

      # brawijaya conversion
      survey_id %in% "brawijaya" ~
        unname(as.numeric(factor(grade, levels = brawijaya_conversion, ordered = TRUE))),

      # limerick
      survey_id %in% "limerick" ~
        unname(as.numeric(factor(grade, levels = limerick_conversion, ordered = TRUE))),
      
      # mef
      survey_id %in% "mef" ~
        unname(as.numeric(factor(grade, levels = mef_conversion, ordered = TRUE))),  
      
      # york_can
      survey_id %in% "york_can" ~
        unname(as.numeric(factor(grade, levels = york_can_conversion, ordered = TRUE))),
    
      # hungary
        survey_id %in% "hungary" ~
          unname(as.numeric(factor(grade, levels = hungary_conversion, ordered = TRUE))),

      # All other universities stay the same
      survey_id %in% c("bournemouth", "bradford", "hasan_kalyoncu", 
                       "la_laguna", "lincoln_1", "lincoln_2", 
                       "macquarie", "queens", "rotterdam", 
                       "southampton", "teesside", "uc_louvain", 
                       "vienna", "western_aus_a", "western_aus_b") ~
        suppressWarnings(as.numeric(grade)),

    )
  )
}

# Applying to df
# ================================================================
smarvus_filtered <- numeric_to_ordinal_grade(smarvus_filtered)
# ================================================================

```
